data.headline: Walmart raises its outlook as inventory grows faster than sales
data.summary: Walmart reported $188.8 billion of third-quarter revenue before Thursday’s opening bell. Sales grew 5.2% from a year earlier and inventory rose 8.1%. Management raised its outlook for full-year earnings and constant-currency sales.

bull.text: Walmart reported a 16% increase in operating income and a 17% rise in global e-commerce sales.

bear.text: Inventory reached $70.6 billion. Walmart attributed the increase to strategic initiatives, seasonal timing and cost inflation. Those factors complicate a direct comparison with sales growth.

watch.text: Management now expects fiscal-year net sales to grow 4.9% to 5.2% in constant currency. That forecast uses a different currency basis from the quarter’s reported revenue growth.

limitations: Walmart reports one retailer’s performance. Its outlook is management guidance. A comparable pre-release analyst estimate remains unavailable.

sources.title: SEC EDGAR · Walmart’s November 19 results filing
